proposals.before: Dong Chuan held Dongchuan as military governor; Hongzhao was appointed his deputy.
proposals.after: Dong Zhang held Dongchuan as military governor; Hongzhao was appointed his deputy.
proposals.reason: Chinese 董璋 is Dong Zhang, not Dong Chuan; 璋 is zhāng.

proposals.before: Meng Zhixiang of Xichuan killed the army supervisor Li Yan. Hongzhao was terrified and begged to return to court, but Dong Chuan refused. Suspicion grew between them—yet Hongzhao treated him openly and without mistrust, and Zhang came to respect him.
proposals.after: Meng Zhixiang of Xichuan killed the army supervisor Li Yan. Hongzhao was terrified and begged to return to court, but Dong Zhang refused. Suspicion grew between them—yet Hongzhao treated him openly and without mistrust, and Zhang came to respect him.
proposals.reason: Replace mistranslated Dong Chuan with Dong Zhang for 璋; keep short Zhang only where the Chinese uses bare 璋.

proposals.before: Later Dong Chuan sent him to court on official business, and Hongzhao was able to leave.
proposals.after: Later Dong Zhang sent him to court on official business, and Hongzhao was able to leave.
proposals.reason: Chinese 璋 refers to Dong Zhang (董璋), not Dong Chuan.

proposals.before: Chonghui reached Fengxiang. Hongzhao received him with elaborate courtesy, entertained him at home, and had his household serve the meal.
proposals.after: Chonghui reached Fengxiang. Hongzhao received him with elaborate courtesy, entertained him at home, and had his wife and concubines serve food and drink.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops 妻妾, which the literal correctly renders as wife and concubines.

proposals.before: Once enthroned, the emperor made Zhao Yinchao Left Remonstrator and Duanming academician; Zhu Mei director of the Bureau of Revenue and direct academician of Military Affairs; Shen Qian commissioner of the Imperial City; Hao commissioner of the Northern Palace Secretariat; and Yanlang commissioner of the Imperial Estates.
proposals.after: Once enthroned, the emperor made Zhaoyin Left Remonstrator and Duanming academician; Zhuanmei director of the Bureau of Revenue and direct academician of Military Affairs; Shenqian commissioner of the Imperial City; Hao commissioner of the Northern Palace Secretariat; and Yanlang commissioner of the Imperial Estates.
proposals.reason: English invents Zhao Yinchao, Zhu Mei, and Shen Qian for 昭胤、專美、審虔, already introduced as Han Zhaoyin, Li Zhuanmei, and Song Shenqian.

proposals.before: In time Zhao Yinchao and Hao became chief councillors, Yanlang deputy, Shen Qian commander of the palace foot guards, and Xue Wenyu director of Appointments and direct academician of Military Affairs.
proposals.after: In time Zhaoyin and Hao became chief councillors, Yanlang deputy, Shenqian commander of the palace foot guards, and Xue Wenyu director of Appointments and direct academician of Military Affairs.
proposals.reason: Same false names Zhao Yinchao and Shen Qian for 昭胤 and 審虔.

proposals.before: Shen Qian held the armies; Zhu Mei and Wenyu shaped policy; Zhao Yinchao, Hao, and Yanlang held the confidential seals.
proposals.after: Shenqian held the armies; Zhuanmei and Wenyu shaped policy; Zhaoyin, Hao, and Yanlang held the confidential seals.
proposals.reason: Correct the false English names Shen Qian, Zhu Mei, and Zhao Yinchao to Shenqian, Zhuanmei, and Zhaoyin.

proposals.before: Yanlang’s faction urged keeping Jingtang in the capital. Zhao Yinchao and Zhu Mei objected: “Jingtang and Zhao Yanshou both married Tang princesses. You cannot hold one and not the other.”
proposals.after: Yanlang’s faction urged keeping Jingtang in the capital. Zhaoyin and Zhuanmei objected: “Jingtang and Zhao Yanshou both married Tang princesses. You cannot hold one and not the other.”
proposals.reason: Zhao Yinchao and Zhu Mei wrongly replace 昭胤 and 專美.

proposals.before: The emperor plotted with Yanlang day and night. Zhu Mei and Wenyu slept in the Zhongxing Hall and were called in for counsel, often until midnight.
proposals.after: The emperor plotted with Yanlang day and night. Zhuanmei and Wenyu slept in the Zhongxing Hall and were called in for counsel, often until midnight.
proposals.reason: Zhu Mei is a false name for 專美 (Zhuanmei / Li Zhuanmei).

proposals.before: When Emperor Min took the throne, he made the Deposed Emperor Beijing commissioner without a formal edict and sent palace attendant Zhao Chuyuan to hurry him on his way.
proposals.after: When Emperor Min took the throne, he made the Deposed Emperor Defender of the Northern Capital without a formal edict and sent palace attendant Zhao Chuyuan to hurry him on his way.
proposals.reason: 北京留守 is the historical office Defender of the Northern Capital, not a commissioner in modern Beijing.

proposals.before: Emperor Min enthroned Hongshi for killing Congrong. Yicheng’s resentment deepened.
proposals.after: When Emperor Min took the throne, Hongshi often boasted of the merit of killing Congrong, and Yicheng’s resentment deepened.
proposals.reason: Chinese 湣帝即位，弘實常以誅從榮功自負 means Emperor Min took the throne and Hongshi boasted of killing Congrong; the idiomatic English wrongly makes Min enthrone Hongshi.

decisions.reason: s0003 Chinese 〈（馮赟附）〉 uses corner brackets as annotation marks; the English sense is only “(With Feng Yun appended)”, so the stray closing 〉 is a punctuation artifact, not meaning.
The same annotation 〈（馮赟附）〉 should not leave a closing 〉 in the literal English; removing it matches the sense without changing the gloss.
s0007 names 董璋; 璋 is zhāng, so “Dong Zhang” is required and “Dong Chuan” is a wrong reading of the given name.
In s0008 the bare 璋 that refuses Hongzhao’s return is the same 董璋; expanding it as “Dong Zhang” is correct, while “Dong Chuan” invents a different name.
s0009 後璋有軍事 continues the same person 董璋; “Dong Zhang” restores the source name and “Dong Chuan” remains wrong.
